sites.name: Crowley JAXPORT Marine Terminal - Jacksonville FL

steps.step: Route to correct building / drop yard

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster point (30.356209, -81.625015 / 2831 Talleyrand Ave) is the
Crowley Main Port Office — an L-shaped office building ringed by employee
parking, confirmed at satellite z19. The office is not the operational yard;
the audited facility is the Crowley Talleyrand container terminal that the
office serves. Wide imagery (z15) shows a continuous container terminal running
roughly 1 km along the west bank of the St. Johns River: container stacks,
chassis/trailer yards, gantry-crane berths, transit-shed warehouses, and a tank
farm at the north end. Web research (crowley.com, jaxport.com) confirms Crowley
runs LNG-powered ConRo ships from JAXPORT's Talleyrand Marine Terminal and that
the north gate was reconstructed during a terminal modernization.

Audited center set to the terminal interior (~30.3544, -81.6239).

fieldNotes.siteIdentification: Pinned address 2831 Talleyrand Ave is the Crowley Main Port Office (L-shaped office building w/ employee lot). The audited facility is the full Crowley Talleyrand container terminal that the office serves - a large ConRo terminal running ~1km along the St. Johns River.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Modernized 'north gate' confirmed in satellite z20 and Street View (2022/2023): a multi-lane covered canopy gate structure with painted yellow lane chevrons and check-in booth modules. Crowley press states the north gate was reconstructed and trucker turn time cut to ~20 min.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Canopied gate has integrated check-in booth modules under/beside the canopy; a separate small booth structure sits near the road - staffed gate operation.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: ~3 inbound lanes visible under the gate canopy with yellow directional chevrons; exit lanes ~2. Counts approximate.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide gate apron and multi-lane canopy provide physical room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Extensive container/chassis stacking yard and trailer parking - many hundreds of containers and trailers visible across the terminal.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Marine terminal - no warehouse-style dock bank; count reflects loading doors on the riverside transit shed at the south end (z17). Low confidence.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale clearly resolved in imagery; common at ports but not confirmed - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail spurs run into the terminal area (visible NW of the gate and along the west edge); Talleyrand has an adjacent intermodal yard (ICTF).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus-scale: gate complex, multiple transit sheds/warehouses, tank farm, container yards and crane-served berths.

sites.name: Crowley Port Everglades Terminal - Fort Lauderdale FL

container terminal in the Southport area of Port Everglades. The roster
coordinates are accurate. Satellite imagery (z15-z21) shows a large container
terminal — container stacks, chassis/trailer yards, gantry-crane berths along
the waterway, and intermodal rail spurs on the west side. Web research
(crowley.com, porteverglades.net, petpev.com) confirms the terminal: 78 acres,
8 lanes, 4 scales, 3 berths, 5,000-FEU yard capacity, rail access.

fieldNotes.siteIdentification: 4300 McIntosh Road = Crowley Port Everglades Terminal, a 78-acre container terminal in Port Everglades' Southport area. Confirmed by imagery + web (crowley.com, porteverglades.net, petpev.com): container stacks, chassis yards, 3 gantry-crane berths, rail spurs. Roster coords accurate.

fieldNotes.guardShack: Check-in booth structures at the covered gate canopy plus the McIntosh Road security checkpoint; staffed (TWIC port access, escort fees collected).
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Web states 8 total lanes; assigned ~4 inbound / ~4 outbound. Exit-lane split flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: 8-lane covered gate with wide aprons - clear room for express/bypass lanes.
fieldNotes.scale: Web confirms 4 scales at the terminal gate complex - scale TRUE (high confidence).
fieldNotes.multiStep: Two-stage entry: outer McIntosh Road port security checkpoint, then the terminal's own multi-lane scaled in-gate - clearly a staged check-in.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Very large container/chassis stacking yard, 5,000 FEU yard capacity per web; hundreds of trailers/containers - banded 50+.

fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus-scale terminal: gate complex, offices, maintenance buildings, multiple container/chassis yards, 3 berths.

fieldNotes.facility: Crowley Jacksonville Cross Dock at 2061 Seaboard Coast Line (SCL) Drive, 32209. The roster's geocoded coordinate (30.324541,-81.663312, GEOMETRIC_CENTER) was WRONG — it pointed at downtown Jacksonville's St. Johns riverfront. fieldNotes.identification: No explicit Crowley nameplate was visible in available Street View, so identification is by strong circumstantial match: it is the only large cross-dock/LTL terminal complex on SCL Drive beside the rail yard in 32209, and its physical profile matches Crowley's published spec exactly (12.1 acres, ~45,580 sq ft of buildings with a 31,500 sq ft long cross-dock, a separate ~10,000 sq ft trailer maintenance building, 150+ trailer yard). Hapag-Lloyd / China Shipping ocean containers in the yard fit an ocean-carrier LCL/cross-dock operation.
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE. Street View (2022-12) shows a chain-link sliding gate across the truck driveway off the east access road.
fieldNotes.guardShack: TRUE (medium confidence). Street View shows a small peaked-roof gatehouse structure beside the entrance lane just inside the gate; satellite z20 confirms a small building footprint at the gate. Listed in uncertainFields because the structure could not be 100% confirmed as a manned booth vs a small office.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 50+ band. Web research states 58 dock doors; satellite confirms a long cross-dock building with dock doors and trailers backed in along both long faces.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: TRUE. The long cross-dock building has dock banks on both opposing long faces — a classic cross-dock through-flow with separate inbound/outbound sides.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 50+. A very large paved trailer drop yard holds well over 100 trailers/tractors; Crowley spec lists 150+ yard capacity.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: TRUE. The campus has the long cross-dock building plus several support buildings, including a separate ~10,000 sq ft trailer maintenance facility.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: TRUE. Wide paved gate apron and abundant unused paved width inside the gate provide room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.railServed: Set false. The site abuts a major rail yard but no dedicated rail spur is clearly visible running into the property; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.confidence: Medium — the cross-dock site is resolved with high spatial confidence (only matching facility on SCL Drive by the rail yard) and the layout matches Crowley's published spec, but no on-site Crowley signage was visible and the roster geocode was badly wrong, so the operator identity rests on circumstantial evidence.

fieldNotes.facility: CrowleyFresh temperature-controlled distribution center, 11401 NW 100th Road, Suite 1, Medley FL. The address is a SUITE — CrowleyFresh occupies one tenant unit (the cold-storage section, 9 refrigerated dock doors per Crowley's spec) within a larger multi-tenant industrial warehouse. Positively identified by multiple CROWLEY reefer trailers backed into the dock face and parked in the yard (Street View 2025-11).
fieldNotes.truckGate: FALSE. No controlled truck entrance. Street View shows open, ungated access from the industrial-park street directly into a shared paved dock court; only a stop sign at the road. No barrier arm, gate, or pinch-point.
fieldNotes.guardShack: FALSE. No guard booth anywhere at the property entrance or dock court.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: FALSE — there is no gate at all.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: FALSE. A single warehouse building; CrowleyFresh shares it with other tenants (FedEx trailers also seen) — multi-tenant, not a multi-building campus.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 50+ band for the whole building. The multi-tenant warehouse has dock doors running along both long (SW and NE) faces with trailers backed in. CrowleyFresh's own suite has 9 refrigerated dock doors per web research; the band reflects the whole building per the rubric (count across all faces). dockDoorCount metric ~52 is an estimate and flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: TRUE. Dock doors are on two opposite long faces of the building (SW and NE), giving physically separate dock clusters.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 10-25 trailers parked in the open court / yard, including CROWLEY reefers; not a dedicated fenced drop lot.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Short open approach from the park street straight into the dock court; no deep internal queue.
fieldNotes.railServed: FALSE. A rail line runs alongside the NE side of the property but no spur enters the building.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Medley is a dense industrial municipality in the Miami metro — Urban.
fieldNotes.coldStorage: Crowley web research: 400,000+ cu ft refrigerated space, a refrigerated dock with 9 access doors, a forced-air pre-cooling chamber (20,000 kg/hr), and four independent temperature-controlled chambers (32-50 F).
fieldNotes.confidence: High for facility identification and the no-gate/no-guard-shack determination (open multi-tenant warehouse, Crowley branding confirmed on docked reefers). Whole-building dock count and lane counts remain overhead/Street-View estimates and are flagged uncertain.
